B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The official MCP documentation says a free Basic Mermaid account works and authentication itself is free. It does not state a separate MCP fee. B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Basic: free. Plus: $10 per user/month billed annually. Premium: $20 per user/month billed annually. Enterprise: custom annual pricing.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The pricing page lists Basic with 15 AI credits, Plus with 300/year, Premium with 2,000/year, and Enterprise with unlimited AI credits. Endpoint metadata describes some AI-backed tools as consuming credits; no MCP-specific per-call price is published.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with an authentication-required error. Its OAuth resource metadata advertises the email scope. Official documentation for the different mcp.mermaid.ai endpoint says every tool call requires a Mermaid login; the endpoint root metadata says some tools need no authentication.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and Mermaid account holder; the available evidence does not document organization-admin controls for this endpoint.

The supplied endpoint probe returned HTTP 401, WWW-Authenticate Bearer metadata, and an unauthorized JSON-RPC error. Its protected-resource documents name a Supabase authorization server and list email as the supported resource scope. The authorization-server metadata advertises authorization_code and refresh_token grants, PKCE methods S256 and plain, Dynamic Client Registration, and token authentication methods client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, and none. Token lifetime and revocation details were not supplied.
C_capabilities.pre_interaction_context_verbatim: HTTP 401; WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="mcp", resource_metadata="https://mcp.mermaidchart.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp", authorization_server="https://ummcsnegloedxcrwlucz.supabase.co/auth/v1/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server". Protected resource scopes_supported: ["email"]. Authorization server scopes_supported: ["openid", "profile", "email", "phone", "offline_access"].
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthorized response captured as JSON-RPC error code -32001, message Unauthorized, with data.error unauthorized and data.error_description Authentication required.

DCR endpoint is https://ummcsnegloedxcrwlucz.supabase.co/auth/v1/oauth/clients/register. Grants: authorization_code, refresh_token. PKCE: S256, plain. Client auth methods: client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, none. Protected resource scopes_supported: email. Authorization server scopes_supported: openid, profile, email, phone, offline_access. The vendor also operates a separately documented host/path with a different published tool count, so endpoint identity and tool-set boundaries need to be kept distinct.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The endpoint’s official root metadata at https://mcp.mermaidchart.com/ names 13 tools. The current official MCP documentation at https://mermaid.ai/docs/ai/mcp-server lists nine tools, for the other documented host mcp.mermaid.ai. mcpserver.lol reported 25 tools from a running server; six names overlap the official endpoint list and 19 catalogue-only names were added as third-party entries. Anchor Terminal also reports 25 live tools. Obot AI describes capabilities but gives no tool count; MCPServers.org describes the connector without a count; ToolJunction lists one tool for the separate chatgpt.mermaid.ai/anthropic/mcp endpoint. The catalogue-only tools may reflect an adjacent or differently configured server surface.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Endpoint instructions say, “Use validate_and_render_mermaid_diagram for all diagram creation and validation.” Tool metadata recommends when to use tools, including calling title generation after rendering and listing projects before creating a diagram. Enforcement is not established by the published endpoint metadata.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The privacy policy says personal data is retained as long as needed for stated purposes and users may request deletion through settings or email. Terms state Basic-tier content may be used to improve services, including training Company AI Tools; trial and paid-tier content is not used to train Mermaid AI models. These are product-wide statements, not MCP-specific controls.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Official documentation says Mermaid MCP can validate and render diagrams and integrate with Mermaid projects. It describes a free Basic account as sufficient for the documented mcp.mermaid.ai endpoint.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Published endpoint metadata declares tools and a broad OAuth/authentication requirement but does not describe enforcement for the privacy, retention, or AI-training statements. The terms and privacy policy are policy commitments; evidence inspected does not establish corresponding MCP-specific technical controls.

contradictions: The input endpoint returned HTTP 401 and its OAuth resource metadata advertises the email scope, while its root metadata says six helper tools are available without a token and describes only some account features as authenticated.

The authorization server metadata supports standard OAuth grants and DCR, while official docs for the other mcp.mermaid.ai endpoint also describe manual API-token authentication. The docs do not establish whether the input endpoint accepts that manual token flow.

The input endpoint root metadata lists 13 tools, while current official documentation for mcp.mermaid.ai lists nine. The documented server is on a different host and may be a different version/surface.
The endpoint metadata’s diagram-management category says full CRUD including delete, but the listed tools contain no delete operation.

mcpserver.lol and Anchor Terminal report 25 tools, including GitHub, Jira, and Notion actions not named in the official endpoint list. Those additional catalogue entries are retained as third-party evidence and may represent a different or expanded server configuration.
observations_for_research: The server instructions specify a preferred primary workflow, while tool metadata also supplies when_to_use and when_not_to_use guidance.
The endpoint publishes auxiliary category and cost labels, but these are not the standard MCP tool annotation hints.
OAuth resource metadata advertises a narrower scope list than the authorization server’s supported scopes list.
The official product documentation and the supplied endpoint use different hosts and list different tool totals.
notes: Checked the prepared links.json, pages/ directory, links_check.txt, and available local code. The endpoint root returned official-looking JSON metadata, while /mcp and /mcp/install evidence returned HTTP 401; schemas and successful tools/list output were therefore unavailable. No public server implementation was found: the Mermaid-Chart/mermaid-mcp link returned 404 and the available plugins copy was incomplete; issue-tracker is unrelated server code. Catalogue-only additions came from mcpserver.lol’s reported live list and should be treated cautiously because its 25-tool list includes adjacent GitHub/Jira/Notion functions. Other unofficial Mermaid MCP repositories were listed but not used as evidence.
